data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary AUR package that downloads prebuilt assets from the official upstream GitHub repository with pinned SHA256 checksums. The PKGBUILD contains no executable code in the global scope, and the package() function only performs standard file installations. The disagreement was solely caused by a transient API error in the Qwen model when reviewing .SRCINFO, not by any security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement between 'inconclusive' and 'safe' was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the Qwen model when attempting to audit .SRCINFO, resulting in an overall inconclusive verdict. The Deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. There is no actual security disagreement.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Implement retry logic for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400/500) to prevent incomplete audits and cascading verdict failures.

Decouple tool execution errors from security verdicts; an API failure on a non-executable metadata file (.SRCINFO) should not force an 'inconclusive' security verdict if the core executable files (PKGBUILD) are successfully audited and found safe.
